deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a heavily corrected prose draft from Riemann's natural-philosophy notes. It continues the previous page's speculative theory of the states of aggregation and then begins a restatement of the Newtonian foundations of mechanics. It has three parts.

(A) End of the aggregation-state scheme. On the previous page Riemann split interatomic causes into two groups. Attractive causes: (1) external pressure, (2) cohesion and adhesion forces, jointly called 'Capillarkräfte'. Repulsive causes: (1) thermic repulsion, (2) chemical repulsion. For the gas he said that thermic repulsion, aided by the chemical, balances the external pressure. This page states the case of the liquid. Thermic repulsion, with the help of the chemical, balances the external pressure. The capillary forces alone, without external pressure, cannot balance the repulsive forces; they show themselves in capillary phenomena. This matches the previous page: in liquids the pressure needed for the solid particles to persist must be supplied externally. A section 'Bei dem festen [Aggregatzustande]' is started but breaks off. The intended content, from the previous page, is that in solids the cohesion forces alone supply the required pressure.

In modern terms this is a qualitative force balance. For a gas or liquid: P_ext + F_capillary = R_thermal + R_chemical, with F_capillary alone < R for liquids. For a solid: F_cohesion alone suffices. No formulas are written.

(B) First draft of the Newtonian hypotheses. 'To explain outer perception (or experience), since Newton, besides the geometric axioms, the following hypotheses are used.'
- (1) Law of inertia. A material body alone in space would either keep its place or move with constant velocity in a straight line. In modern notation: if there are no other bodies, d^2x/dt^2 = 0, so x(t) = x0 + v0 t.
- Riemann's remark: this law cannot be derived from the principle of sufficient reason. That a body continues its motion must have a cause, which can be sought only in the inner state of matter.
- (2) is omitted in this draft.
- (3) is struck through and rewritten: at every place in space, at every instant, there are causes (forces) determined in magnitude and direction.

(C) Second, reworked list. It begins: 'This cause Newton seeks [reading uncertain] in the state of motion of a substance spread through infinite space.' This alludes to Newton's speculations about an aether as the cause of gravity.
- (1) All changes of place of ponderable bodies occur continuously: x(t) is continuous.
- (2) Every (dead) ponderable body, independently of any external force, continues at each following instant the motion it had at the previous one. This is inertia in an infinitesimal-step formulation: the velocity persists unless something changes it.
- (3) At every place of space, at every instant, there exists a cause determined in magnitude and direction which [changes] the motion of every ponderable body there. That is, a vector field F(x,t) acting on any body at x.

The sentence breaks off. The next page continues it in a cleaner draft. There, force/acceleration is a constant called mass, forces combine by the parallelogram rule, and the field is an inverse-square field whose strength times r^2 is called the mass. This leads into Riemann's known programme of explaining gravitation and light through a space-filling substance ('Stoff') that flows into ponderable atoms.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there are no computations. The text is a draft with incomplete sentences: 'Bei dem festen' breaks off, item 2 is missing from the first list, and item 3 of the second list is unfinished.

Calling Newton's first law a 'hypothesis' needing a cause in the inner state of matter is a philosophical stance, not a correctness issue. Attributing to Newton an aether-motion explanation of the cause is historically defensible only for Newton's speculative Queries and letters, not the Principia.

results.what: Qualitative force-balance scheme for gas/liquid/solid states: external pressure and capillary (cohesion/adhesion) forces versus thermal and chemical repulsion. In liquids the capillary forces alone cannot balance repulsion; in solids cohesion alone can.
results.modern_name: Pre-kinetic molecular-force theory of aggregation states (compare Laplace/Poisson capillarity, internal-pressure ideas)
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace, Poisson, Gauss (capillarity); general 19th-century molecular physics

results.what: Restatement of the Newtonian axioms (inertia, continuity of motion, a force field defined at each point and instant), with the remark that inertia is not derivable from the principle of sufficient reason and needs a cause in the inner state of matter.
results.modern_name: Newton's laws of motion / field concept of force; Riemann's aether-based natural philosophy
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (1687); Riemann's own fragments 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' and 'Gravitation und Licht' (published posthumously in his Werke, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: These are drafts of material closely related to Riemann's published natural-philosophy fragments (Werke, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'). The page has no mathematics, only qualitative physics and a restatement of Newtonian principles. It is of minor interest for the genesis of those fragments.

checkable.sympy: x0, v0, t = symbols('x0 v0 t'); diff(x0 + v0*t, t, 2) == 0
checkable.asserts: Uniform rectilinear motion x = x0 + v0*t has zero acceleration (law of inertia as formalised on the page).

checkable.sympy: t = symbols('t'); f = Function('x'); dsolve(Eq(f(t).diff(t, 2), 0), f(t))
checkable.asserts: The general solution of x'' = 0 is x = C1 + C2*t: a body free of forces stays at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read 'Bei dem liquiden Aggregatzustande ist die thermische Repulsion [-und-] mit Hülfe der chemischen im Stande dem äusseren Drucke das Gleichgewicht zu halten', not 'die chemische Repulsion'. This parallels the gas case on the previous page.

'Die {+Capillar+}[-...-] Kräfte ... allein (ohne äusseren Druck)' is better read as 'Die Capillarkräfte allein (ohne äusseren Druck) sind nicht im Stande den Repulsivkräften das Gleichgewicht zu halten, sie äussern sich in den Capillarerscheinungen'.
'muss [?] eine Ursache haben' is likely 'muss sie eine Ursache haben'.
'Die Ursache [?] stellt Newton in der Bewegungsform' is likely 'Diese Ursache sucht Newton in der Bewegungsform eines ... unendlichen Raum verbreiteten Stoffes' (reading uncertain).
'Alle ... {+Orts+} ponderablen Körpers! erfolgen' is better read as 'Alle Ortsveränderungen ponderabler Körper erfolgen nach Stetigkeit'.

Item '1, Jeder materielle Körper würde, wenn er sich im Raume ganz allein befände, ... seinen Ort in demselben nicht verändern oder sich mit unveränderlicher Geschwindigkeit in gerader Linie durch denselben bewegen': the interlinear 'jeder Körper' is a variant insertion, not a doubled subject.
